unit.why: A brief anecdote: R. Zusya and his brother R. Elimelekh argue whether humility or contemplation of God's greatness comes first, and the Maggid of Mezritch decides between them. It is minimal but narrated, and its substance is a teaching.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מפי הקדוש המנוח הרב מוה״ר זוסיא
stories.summary_en: R. Zusya relates that he and his brother R. Elimelekh disputed whether one should first attain lowliness of spirit or first contemplate God's greatness; the Maggid of Mezritch ruled that both are valid but that beginning with self-lowliness is the higher rung.

quotes: שיהיה האדם מקודם שפל רוח לתכליתו
מדרגה זו שחושב קודם שפלות עצמו
tags.why: Humility (שפלות) is the subject of the dispute and of the ruling
Contemplating the Creator's greatness is the alternative path to humility
The point of the story is the correct order of acquiring virtues

quotes: ושאלו את הה״מ ממעזריטש וצוק"ל שיכריע ביניהם
tags.why: The disciples bring their dispute to their master, who decides it

quotes: היה מתווכח עם אחיו המפורסם מוהר״ר אלימלך
tags.why: The dispute is between two Hasidic brothers, both disciples
Zusya's brother is a character, though he is himself a tzaddik
The anecdote mainly serves as a vehicle for an ethical-devotional teaching

tags.why: Framed as told orally by R. Zusya
